title: Tenant Alignment Autoscaler and Fallback Guardbook — PRD (draft)
summary: Draft PRD for a tenant-aligned autoscaler that enforces isolation curves and a deterministic fallback guardbook for Dedicated capacity. Combines adaptive per-tenant scaling with negotiated transient burst lanes and a clear ops-facing fallback flow to minimize noisy neighbor regressions while preserving predictable SLA behavior.
background_and_problem: Customers on Dedicated ask for finer-grained predictability: reserved pools work but are brittle under bursty demand; full hard isolation is expensive. Current autoscalers treat pools uniformly which leads to noisy-neighbor incidents (tail latency spikes, preemption thrash). We need a design that: (1) automatically allocates headroom to tenants based on historical and short-window signals, (2) provides short-duration negotiated burst lanes with economic limits, and (3) defines a simple, auditable fallback guardbook for graceful degradation with clear tenant-facing semantics.
goals:
- Reduce incidence of tail-latency/noisy-neighbor events by 60% for multi-tenant Dedicated pools.
- Provide bounded burst capacity that can be requested programmatically with clear billing and eviction contracts.
- Give SRE/operators deterministic playbook for fallbacks, with automated steps for safe traffic migration and warm-reallocation.
- Make tenant autoscale behavior explainable in Console (per-tenant headroom curve, recent grabs, eviction traces).
non_goals:
- Replace customer-managed hard isolation (VPC-only) — that remains an option.
- Solve long-running batch jobs bursting for days — this design targets seconds-to-minutes microbursts and predictable scale events.
- Full market-level burst-auction economics — we propose simple credit/cap model first.
user_stories: As a ML infra engineer, I want a tenant-level autoscaler that reserves a safety band so my latency SLOs don't spike during neighbor bursts.
As a product reliability owner, I want to let my service request short bursts (30s-5m) for peak traffic and have clear cost/eviction guarantees.
As an SRE, I want a deterministic fallback sequence that the control plane will follow during capacity pressure so I can automate remediation runbooks.
As an account manager, I want a UI summary showing recent bursts and whether burst usage hit contractual caps for billing/renewal conversations.
proposed_solution_overview: Introduce 'Tenant Alignment Autoscaler' (TAA) and 'Fallback Guardbook' (FG). TAA maintains a per-tenant headroom curve (percent of pool compute) derived from long-term commit + short-term demand signal. FG is an ordered set of deterministic actions applied when pool utilization crosses thresholds: graded throttles, soft-fallback (route to lower-fidelity model or queued requests), local preemption of opportunistic workloads, and finally tenant-level eviction per contract. Add a negotiated ephemeral-burst API that issues short-lived burst tokens deducted from a tenant's burst credit bucket.
key_components:
- Headroom estimator: combines reserve commitments, recent QPS, token-based rate of requests, and model memory (KV cache reuse).
- Burst credit ledger: per-tenant ephemeral credit that decays and replenishes on contract terms.
- Admission & placement: scheduler that slices pool according to headroom curve and fits model variants to available GPU memory.
- Guardbook FSM: thresholded policy with explicit observable triggers and prioritized action list.
- Console UI surfaces: headroom graph, burst credit balance, last fallback trace.
config_examples: example 1: conservative e-com tenant: min_headroom_pct=12, max_headroom_pct=30, aggressiveness=low, burst_policy=metered-credits
example 2: dev sandbox tenant: min_headroom_pct=3, max_headroom_pct=10, aggressiveness=high, burst_policy=best-effort (no credits)
example 3: enterprise with committed reserve: min_headroom_pct=25, max_headroom_pct=55, aggressiveness=medium, burst_policy=explicit-paid-burst
scheduling_and_placement: Scheduler uses two-stage placement: (A) hard-slice for reserved baseline (commitment), (B) soft-slice for dynamic headroom. When a burst token is granted, scheduler attempts to co-locate with cached KV state for that tenant; if not possible, it uses quantized model variants (quant4/8) to fit. Placement respects affinity and soft isolation fences to reduce noisy neighbor interference. We add a cheap 'probe' allocation for 5s to warm KV caches before granting full burst.
isolation_controls_and_fairness: Isolation is implemented as tunable curves per tenant: headroom curve (pct of pool vs. time window) and momentary cap (max concurrent shards). Fairness logic ensures opportunistic workloads are the first to be preempted; preemption order is deterministic and documented. For multi-tenant colliding bursts, we apply proportional reduction based on configured eviction_priority. The Console will surface 'fairness score' and 'recent preemptions' for transparency.
fallback_guardbook_sequence:
Trigger thresholds: green (<70%), yellow (70-90%), red (>90%).
On yellow: begin soft-denial for best-effort requests, reduce allowed burst grants, start probe reclaims.
On red: enact ordered actions: 1) throttle new burst token issuance; 2) preempt opportunistic/spot workloads for reclaim; 3) degrade model fidelity for overflow routes (fall back to smaller model_variant or cached responses); 4) route non-essential routes to dedicated backup region or queue with SLA degrade; 5) last resort: evict lowest-priority tenants according to contract. Each action emits an event to the trace log and posts to tenant's activity stream in Console.
observability_and_metrics: Per-tenant: headroom_pct, burst_tokens_granted, burst_tokens_used, preemptions_count, tail_latency_95/99, eviction_count. Pool-level: utilization_pct, number_of_active_bursts, average_probe_warm_duration. Alerts: sustained red for >2min triggers automated runbook and email to oncall. Integrations: export to Prometheus and to Console time-series with trace links to request ids.
ops_playbook_and_runbook_excerpt:
- Alert fires: pool_red_high.
- Step 1 (automated): reduce burst issuance; run preempt reclaim script.
- Step 2 (automated): reroute selected low-priority routes to backup region.
- Step 3 (manual): if >1 eviction in 5m, SRE evaluates contract impacts and notifies Customer Success.
- Post-mortem tags: root cause (hotness/recurring-burst/buggy-client) and mitigation (increase min_headroom, adjust burst_policy).
Runbook links: slack #dedicated-ops, GH runbook scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-ops/tree/evac-scripts
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: internal dogfood on non-critical pool (2 weeks) with default conservative curves.
Phase 1: opt-in beta for 10 customers, UI visibility + manual revoke. Monitor metrics for 4 weeks.
Phase 2: graduated defaults and enable automatic headroom tuning for low-risk tenants.
Phase 3: GA with billing integration for paid bursts and SLO-linked defaults.
Rollback: disable burst issuance and revert to current autoscaler behavior (keep reserved baseline).
metrics_success_criteria: Reduce pool-level 99th latency tail events attributed to neighbor interference by 60% vs baseline over 30d.
Successful automated reclaim on yellow->green transitions in <45s in 90% of incidents.
No more than 1 unjustified eviction per 100 tenant-months during beta.
Beta customers report clear visibility in Console and understand billing for bursts (survey).
risks_and_mitigation: Overly aggressive preemption that impacts paid workloads — mitigate: enforce eviction_priority and require explicit opt-in for forced preemption in contracts.
Incorrect headroom estimation causing oscillation — mitigate: add dampening, min-duration for changes, and a probe-based warmup step.
Complexity for customers — mitigate: reasonable defaults, UI explanations, and one-click rollback.
open_questions: Should burst credits be bill-on-grant or bill-on-use? (ops prefers bill-on-use; sales prefers bill-on-grant for predictability)
What is acceptable default aggressiveness for enterprise vs self-serve customers?
How do we expose quantized model fallback options without leaking internal variant mapping in UI?
